title: Computational response to peer review
subtitle: Manuscript NNN-NNNNN — drafted for the authors, not final

sections.heading: R2.C8 — is the interfacial Pt genuinely metallic Pt0?
paragraphs: Reviewer comment (verbatim): "... is it possible that the 'Pt0 near the interface' is in fact a Ptd+ species ...".

We computed CO adsorption energies and Bader charges for a metallic Pt cluster and an oxidized single-atom reference on anatase TiO2(101), using the manuscript's settings (PBE+U(Ti 3d)=4 eV, ENCUT 400 eV, Gamma-centred 2x2x1, spin-polarized). Energies are relative to gas-phase CO and the clean slab; see Table 1 and Figures 1-2.

Outcome: addresses-with-limitations. The interfacial Pt is near-neutral and retains metallic Pt-Pt bonds, consistent with the manuscript's Pt0 assignment; the charge difference is below what Bader alone can resolve, so the claim rests on the CO-stretch and binding trends shown in Figures 1-2.
